result:
Phase: Implement from a written spec (~12 files)

Model and effort: sonnet, medium — switch for this session only via `/model` then `s`.

Boundary: this recommendation stays in your context until the next `/clear`. If you're currently in a planning session (opus/fable at high effort), write the plan to a file first, then `/clear` before switching — otherwise the model/effort change re-processes that whole warm context.

Delegate: nothing structural — keep the implementation itself in the main model. Push read-only work (running tests, reading logs, fetching docs) to Haiku subagents if `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` + `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` are set.

Done when: all files in the spec are touched, tests pass, and `npm run lint` (or equivalent) is clean.

You give up: sonnet/medium occasionally needs a retry on trickier files that opus/xhigh would one-shot — cheaper in aggregate per the bench (17% of opus/xhigh cost, same pass rate).

Escalate when: a specific file/step fails and a fix attempt doesn't resolve it — then go to opus, medium, then xhigh if that still fails. Don't preemptively raise effort.

Phase: Review a diff (six files, in a repo you know well).

Model and effort: opus, low. Switch with `s` in the `/model` picker.

Boundary: this recommendation stays in your current context until your next `/clear`, so route just before one to spend least. Switching model/effort now re-processes whatever's already in this context — if that's small, the cost is negligible.

Delegate: nothing — this is small enough to review directly, no subagent needed.

Done when: every finding carries a file:line and you can trace the code path it describes.

You give up: a shot at catching subtler issues that only surface at higher effort — acceptable here since the bench found all five planted defects in this exact six-file-diff scenario at low effort, in 3 turns.

Escalate when: opus at low misses something you can point to, or the diff turns out larger/less familiar than expected — then go to opus, high (measured at 3.3x the cost for the same five defects on this case, so only worth it if low actually falls short).
